In recent weeks, President Donald Trump has ramped up his threat to dispatch National Guard troops into American cities -- with Chicago and Portland, Oregon, being the most recent examples.
Unlike the deployment of the National Guard either at the order or request of a state's governor, Trump has sought to federalize the Guard against the will of the governors of Illinois and Oregon.
And in both cases, Trump is seeking to deploy National Guard members from other states.
Under U.S. law, the Guard can be called to active duty by a president in such cases as invasion by a foreign country, rebellion against the federal government or being unable to execute federal laws.
But in doing so, troops are limited to protecting federal buildings and federal personnel unless the president invokes the Insurrection Act, which he has not done.
